hypotheses.justification: `psc` never reads coefficients of the left input above the left bound. In `subresultantMatrix p q m n j` (Subresultant/Basic.lean:67), a `p`-block entry is `if k ≤ i+j ∧ i+j ≤ k+m then p.coeff (i+j-k) else 0`, so the index is always ≤ m. With `coeff_reductum` (`(p.reductum k).coeff i = if i < k then p.coeff i else 0`), `ext` + `Fin.addCases` + `simp [subresultantMatrix, coeff_reductum]` + `omega` give `subresultantMatrix P Q m N j = subresultantMatrix (P.reductum (m+1)) Q m N j` for every P, Q, N. Hence `psc P Q m N j = psc (P.reductum (m+1)) Q m N j`. Proof without `hm`: set `p' := p.reductum (m+1)`. It satisfies `(p'.map f).natDegree ≤ m` by `natDegree_map_le` and `natDegree_reductum_lt`. Apply the current theorem to `p'` (the other hypotheses do not involve p). Then rewrite: `psc p q m N j = psc p' q m N j`; `p'.coeff m = p.coeff m` by `coeff_reductum`; and `p'.map f = (p.map f).reductum (m+1)` by `reductum_map`, so `psc (p'.map f) _ m n j = psc (p.map f) _ m n j` by the same truncation fact. No degenerate case is excluded: the truncation argument holds for all p, m, j, including p = 0. Sanity check: p = X^2, q = 1, m = 1, n = j = 0, N = 1 gives 0 on both sides.
